questions.stem: What energy transformation takes place in a DC motor?
questions.explanation: A DC motor converts electrical energy into rotational kinetic energy. Some energy is also wasted as heat due to friction and resistance in the coil.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a component of a simple DC motor?
questions.explanation: A simple DC motor consists of a rotating coil (armature), permanent magnets, a split-ring commutator, and carbon brushes. A transformer is not part of a DC motor.

questions.stem: Why does the coil in a DC motor rotate?

options.text: Because the commutator spins it mechanically
Because the two sides of the coil experience forces in opposite directions, creating a turning effect
Because the brushes push the coil around
Because the permanent magnets push it around

questions.explanation: Current flows in opposite directions on each side of the coil. By Fleming's left-hand rule, this means each side experiences a force in the opposite direction, creating a couple (turning effect) that makes the coil rotate.

questions.stem: What is the function of the carbon brushes in a DC motor?

options.text: To maintain electrical contact between the power supply and the rotating commutator
To increase the speed of rotation

questions.explanation: Carbon brushes press against the spinning commutator to maintain electrical contact, allowing current to flow from the external power supply into the rotating coil continuously.

questions.stem: How can the speed of a DC motor be increased?

options.text: By increasing the current or using stronger magnets

questions.explanation: The speed of a DC motor can be increased by increasing the current (greater force on the coil), using stronger magnets (greater magnetic flux density), or increasing the number of turns on the coil.

questions.stem: How can the direction of rotation of a DC motor be reversed?

options.text: By increasing the number of turns on the coil
By reversing the current direction or reversing the magnetic field direction

questions.explanation: The direction of rotation can be reversed by either reversing the current direction or reversing the magnetic field (swapping the magnets). Reversing both would keep the rotation the same.

questions.stem: What happens to the coil of a DC motor when it reaches the vertical position (perpendicular to the field)?

options.text: The coil sides are parallel to the field so the force is zero, but momentum carries it past this point
The force on the coil is at its maximum
The current in the coil doubles

questions.explanation: When the coil is vertical, its sides are parallel to the magnetic field, so the motor effect force is zero. However, the coil's momentum carries it past this dead point, and the commutator reverses the current to continue rotation.
